Standardised precipitation indices: SPI and SPEI

Source: R/calc_std_index.R
calc_std_index.Rd

Computes the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) or the Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) for every unit, at one or more accumulation scales in months. Replaces compute_spi() of climatic4economist, compute_spei() and compute_water_balance().

Usage

calc_std_index(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
calc_std_index(
  x,
  scale,
  index = c("spi", "spei"),
  pet = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  chunk = "auto",
  .parallel = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Monthly precipitation (or water balance), wide from extract_*() or long.

...

Further arguments of the methods; the table method takes none.

scale

Accumulation periods in months, e.g. c(1, 3, 6).

index

"spi" or "spei".

pet

For the SPEI, monthly potential evapotranspiration for the same units and dates, in the same unit as x.

id

Optional name of the unit identifier column.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

chunk

"auto" splits the work by unit when it would not fit in memory; a whole number forces that many units per chunk; FALSE never splits.

.parallel

When TRUE, fit the series with furrr, following the user's future::plan().

Value

A long c4e_tbl with one column per scale, e.g. spi_3, registered with the index and scale.

Details

The data must be monthly. Daily rasters are aggregated first with aggregate_time(), before extraction.

For the SPEI, give potential evapotranspiration in pet (a table of the same units and months): the water balance is precipitation minus its absolute value, matched by unit and date, so ERA5's convention of negative evaporation needs no change. Without pet, x is taken to be the water balance already.

Each series is fitted on its own with SPEI::spi() or SPEI::spei().

See also

calc_std_threshold()

Other indicators: calc_condition(), calc_heatwave(), calc_par(), calc_percentile(), calc_percentile_day(), calc_spell(), calc_spell_excess(), calc_spell_percentile(), calc_std_threshold(), calc_threshold_day()

Examples

pre <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "pre_monthly.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read pre_monthly: pre [mm/month], monthly, 1984-01-01 to 2023-12-01, 480 layers
#> (synthetic).
survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon)
points <- georef_coord(coord, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

extract_by_coord(pre, points) |>
  calc_std_index(scale = 3)
#> # A tibble: 5,760 × 6
